rituals.title: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
rituals.name: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
rituals.hook: Shift: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
rituals.hook_internal: Shift: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Keep Event → Predict Different → Speak Plurals
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Keep Event → Predict Different → Speak Plurals
rituals.goal: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
rituals.mission: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
rituals.challenge: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
rituals.immediate_need: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Catastrophic prediction

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Keep Event — Keep the event fixed. Three Worlds — widen gaze.
2. Invent — Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Predict Different — Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next. Three Worlds — challenge answer.
4. Earliest — Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Speak Plurals — Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy. Three Worlds — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Speak Plurals.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
rituals.formula_flow: Keep Event → Invent → Predict Different → Earliest → Speak Plurals
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not multiply theories when an urgent practical response is already clear.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
rituals.safety_notes:

rituals.title: ADD THE PREFIX
rituals.name: ADD THE PREFIX
rituals.hook: Twist: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.hook_internal: Twist: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Prefix Thought → Check Command → Resume Task
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Prefix Thought → Check Command → Resume Task
rituals.goal: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.mission: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.challenge: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.immediate_need: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Prefix Thought — Take the exact thought and place these words before it: ‘I am noticing my mind produce…’ Say the complete sentence once at ordinary speed. Add Prefix — breathe naturally.
2. Check Command — Notice what remains true and what loses command authority. Add Prefix — pick action.
3. Resume Task — Carry on with the next chosen task while the sentence exists nearby. Add Prefix — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Resume Task.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.formula_flow: Prefix Thought → Check Command → Resume Task
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Drop the wording if it feels mocking, unreal, or destabilising.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Ask Danger → Answer M → Respect
rituals.goal: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.mission: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.challenge: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.immediate_need: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Values, meaning & loss

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Ask Danger — Ask what danger the thought is trying to prevent. Thanks Mind — move slowly.
2. Thank Intention — Offer a precise thank-you for that intention.
3. Answer M — Then answer: ‘I’m not signing this instruction.’ Choose a matching what matters to you action that keeps any useful caution but rejects the controlling move. Thanks Mind — split duty.
4. Respect — Respect the alarm; decline the contract. Thanks Mind — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Respect.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.formula_flow: Ask Danger → Thank Intention → Answer M → Respect
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not dismiss warnings that point to concrete and immediate danger.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
rituals.name: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
rituals.hook: Catch: Give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.hook_internal: Catch: Give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Place Thought → Return Eyes → Allow Departure
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Place Thought → Return Eyes → Allow Departure
rituals.goal: Give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.mission: Give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.challenge: Give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.immediate_need: Give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Rigid beliefs, labels & stories

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Place Thought — Place the thought on something already moving: a bus passing, a leaf in drainage water, subtitles leaving a screen. Thought Departures — soften shoulders.
2. Watch Arrival — Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. Return Eyes — When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one stationary object. Thought Departures — allow opposite.
4. Allow Departure — Another vehicle may come; none owns the station. Thought Departures — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Allow Departure.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ I can give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.formula_flow: Place Thought → Watch Arrival → Return Eyes → Allow Departure
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop imagery if it increases detachment from surroundings.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: PASSENGER THOUGHT
rituals.hook: Look: You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.
rituals.hook_internal: Look: You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Choose Time → Keep Hands → Who Drove?
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Choose Time → Keep Hands → Who Drove?
rituals.goal: You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.
rituals.mission: You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.
rituals.challenge: You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.
rituals.immediate_need: You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Time — Choose one two-minute action that matters. Passenger Thought — move slowly.
2. Ride Passenger — Invite the thought to ride in the passenger seat—audible, uncomfortable, unedited.
3. Keep Hands — Hold hands on the action wheel and complete the movement while it talks. Passenger Thought — pick action.
4. Who Drove? — At the destination, Notice who actually drove. Passenger Thought — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Who Drove?.

rituals.hook: Bet: Capacity grows sideways, not through force.

rituals.challenge: Capacity grows sideways, not through force.
rituals.immediate_need: Capacity grows sideways, not through force.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Values, meaning & loss

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Capacity grows sideways, not through force.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Locate Unwanted — Locate the unwanted sensation. Make Wider — loosen hands.
2. Find Edges — Find its edges.
3. Soften Muscles — Soften the muscles around—not inside—it. Make Wider — split duty.
4. Include Neutral — Include one neutral body area and one external sound in awareness.
5. Enlarging — You are enlarging the room, not evicting the guest. Make Wider — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Enlarging.

rituals.safety:

rituals.name: PAIN PLUS THE FIGHT
rituals.hook: Play: Separate the wound from the fist wrapped around it.
rituals.hook_internal: Play: Separate the wound from the fist wrapped around it.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Make Two Lanes → Catch The Fight → Drop One Fight
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Make Two Lanes → Catch The Fight → Drop One Fight

rituals.challenge: Separate the wound from the fist wrapped around it.
rituals.immediate_need: Separate the wound from the fist wrapped around it.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Self-blame, guilt & shame

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Separate the wound from the fist wrapped around it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Make Two Lanes — Imagine two lanes: WHAT HURTS and WHAT RESISTANCE ADDS. Pain Plus — soften shoulders.
2. Keep The Hurt — In the first lane, picture the raw sensation or fact.
3. Catch The Fight — In the second lane, name demands, self-attack, bracing, and impossible arguments with reality. Pain Plus — split duty.
4. Drop One Fight — Release one item from the resistance lane while respecting the hurt. Pain Plus — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Drop One Fight.

✓ I kept the useful lesson and dropped the attack.

rituals.safety:

Do not use acceptance language to tolerate abuse, injustice, or untreated symptoms.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Perfectionism & performance pressure

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Ordinary — Choose one ordinary activity. Enter Action — feel support.
2. Place Vision — Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. Leave Re — When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself. Enter Action — allow opposite.
4. Stay Activity — Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Participation — Participation, not perfect focus, is the target. Enter Action — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Participation.

rituals.title: THE ATTENTION BOUNCER
rituals.name: THE ATTENTION BOUNCER
rituals.hook: Flip: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.hook_internal: Flip: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Spot Arrival → Set Budget → Return Door
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Spot Arrival → Set Budget → Return Door
rituals.goal: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.mission: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.challenge: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.immediate_need: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Spot Arrival — Notice the next thought without following it. Attention Bouncer — move slowly.
2. Stamp Access — Stamp it REQUESTED, RELEVANT, or UNINVITED.
3. Set Budget — Give only the chosen category a short timer; let the others wait without argument. Attention Bouncer — notice detail.
4. Return Door — When the timer ends, return to the task or deliberately admit one new thought. Attention Bouncer — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Return Door.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.formula_flow: Spot Arrival → Stamp Access → Set Budget → Return Door
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the labels become a checking ritual or make urgent action harder.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.hook: Shift: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.

rituals.challenge: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
rituals.immediate_need: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
rituals.trigger_play_time:

GOAL
Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
rituals.play_the_loop:

rituals.name: THE 2% SOFTENING
rituals.hook: Notice: Your face can send the nervous system a quieter memo.
rituals.hook_internal: Notice: Your face can send the nervous system a quieter memo.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Release Forehead → Hold Neutral → Ask Whether
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Release Forehead → Hold Neutral → Ask Whether
rituals.goal: Your face can send the nervous system a quieter memo.
rituals.mission: Your face can send the nervous system a quieter memo.
rituals.challenge: Your face can send the nervous system a quieter memo.
rituals.immediate_need: Your face can send the nervous system a quieter memo.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Your face can send the nervous system a quieter memo.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Release Forehead — Without forcing happiness, release the forehead, loosen the eyes, and lift the mouth corners by only two percent. Softening Still — soften shoulders.
2. Keep Expression — Keep the expression believable.
3. Hold Neutral — Hold it while looking at one neutral object. Softening Still — name sensation.
4. Ask Whether — Ask whether defence changed by even half a notch. Softening Still — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Ask Whether.

rituals.title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
rituals.name: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
rituals.hook: Look: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
rituals.hook_internal: Look: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Set Code → Reverse Code → Claim Control
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Set Code → Reverse Code → Claim Control
rituals.goal: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
rituals.mission: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
rituals.challenge: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
rituals.immediate_need: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and look at one fixed object. Say the order once. Play Body — hear sound.
2. Run Order — Perform A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — Perform C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, return to neutral and restart instead of speeding up. Play Body — name sensation.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the whole code stop. Play Body — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Claim Control.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
rituals.formula_flow: Set Code → Run Order → Reverse Code → Claim Control
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not play while driving, moving through hazards, dizzy, injured, or unable to stay oriented.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE
rituals.hook: Bet: Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.
rituals.hook_internal: Bet: Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Stop Nonessential → Observe Facts → Skip Negotiation
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Stop Nonessential → Observe Facts → Skip Negotiation

rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Urges, impulses & cravings

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Stop Nonessential — S — stop every nonessential movement. Four Letter — feel support.
2. Take Physical — T — take one physical step back.
3. Observe Facts — O — observe facts, sensations, and the strongest impulse. Four Letter — name feeling.
4. Proceed Safely — P — proceed with the smallest safe move that will still make sense in an hour.
5. Skip Negotiation — Do not negotiate with momentum between letters. Four Letter — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Skip Negotiation.

rituals.plain:
THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE

TRIGGER
Urges, impulses & cravings

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

GOAL
Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.

1. Stop Nonessential — S — stop every nonessential movement. Four Letter — feel support.
2. Take Physical — T — take one physical step back.
3. Observe Facts — O — observe facts, sensations, and the strongest impulse. Four Letter — name feeling.
4. Proceed Safely — P — proceed with the smallest safe move that will still make sense in an hour.
5. Skip Negotiation — Do not negotiate with momentum between letters. Four Letter — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Skip Negotiation.

WIN SIGNAL
✓ Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.

FORMULA FLOW
Stop Nonessential → Take Physical → Observe Facts → Proceed Safely → Skip Negotiation

rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Hold distress and safety in the same frame.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Stable — Choose a stable anchor such as feet on the floor or a fixed sound. Foot Here — press feet.
2. Keep Most — Keep most attention there while allowing a small edge of distress into awareness.
3. Anchor Verify — Verify the anchor remains present. Foot Here — name sensation.
4. Adjust — Adjust the ratio until both can coexist without losing choice. Foot Here — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Adjust.

rituals.title: EXHALE IN CHAPTERS
rituals.name: EXHALE IN CHAPTERS
rituals.hook: Notice: A large release can become several manageable ones.
rituals.hook_internal: Notice: A large release can become several manageable ones.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Let Air → Keep Face → Wait Body
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Let Air → Keep Face → Wait Body
rituals.goal: A large release can become several manageable ones.
rituals.mission: A large release can become several manageable ones.
rituals.challenge: A large release can become several manageable ones.
rituals.immediate_need: A large release can become several manageable ones.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A large release can become several manageable ones.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Let Air — Instead of one continuous out-breath, let air leave in three soft portions with tiny unforced spaces between. Exhale Chapters — breathe naturally.
2. Keep Face — Keep the face loose and never push to empty. Exhale Chapters — name sensation.
3. Wait Body — After the final segment, wait for the body’s next inhale rather than grabbing it. Exhale Chapters — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Wait Body.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ A large release can become several manageable ones.
rituals.formula_flow: Let Air → Keep Face → Wait Body
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Resume normal breathing if segmentation causes urgency or tingling.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.hook: Check: Observe experience without appointing a headline.
rituals.hook_internal: Check: Observe experience without appointing a headline.

rituals.goal: Observe experience without appointing a headline.
rituals.mission: Observe experience without appointing a headline.
rituals.challenge: Observe experience without appointing a headline.
rituals.immediate_need: Observe experience without appointing a headline.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Rigid beliefs, labels & stories

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Observe experience without appointing a headline.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Open Field — Open Field with sight, sound, sensation, and thought available at once. Let Field — widen gaze.
2. Whatever — Notice whatever becomes prominent, then what replaces it.
3. Let All Arrive — Do not select, rank, or hold any item. Let Field — allow opposite.
4. Track Changing — Track the changing editorial order for one minute. Let Field — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Track Changing.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL

rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Let Field — Let the field choose its next foreground. No Favourite — soften shoulders.
2. Pleasant — Pleasant, unpleasant, dull, or vivid—offer each the same brief hospitality.
3. Include Movement — When preference reaches to grip or reject, include that movement too. No Favourite — notice detail.
4. End Whole — End by noticing the whole room at once. No Favourite — next action.

⚡ FINISH — End Whole.

rituals.hook: Pause: Move awareness through an hourglass.

rituals.goal: Move awareness through an hourglass.

rituals.challenge: Move awareness through an hourglass.

rituals.trigger_play_time:

Body-state misreading

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Move awareness through an hourglass.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Acknowledge — First, acknowledge the full weather of the moment. Expand Gather — press feet.
2. Breathe Small — Next, gather attention around breathing as a small centre.
3. Widen Whole — Finally, widen to the whole body and surrounding space. Expand Gather — notice detail.
4. Spend — Spend roughly one minute in each shape.
5. Carry Final — Carry the final wide frame into your next movement. Expand Gather — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Carry Final.

rituals.title: FOUR PARTS OF ONE STEP
rituals.name: FOUR PARTS OF ONE STEP
rituals.hook: Probe: Walking can become a moving attention track.
rituals.hook_internal: Probe: Walking can become a moving attention track.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Place Weight → Thought → Finish Walking
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Place Weight → Thought → Finish Walking
rituals.goal: Walking can become a moving attention track.
rituals.mission: Walking can become a moving attention track.
rituals.challenge: Walking can become a moving attention track.
rituals.immediate_need: Walking can become a moving attention track.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Walking can become a moving attention track.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Place Weight — Slow enough to distinguish lift, travel, place, and weight transfer. Four Parts — move slowly.
2. Follow Events — Follow those four events through several steps.
3. Thought — When thought pulls away, rejoin at whichever phase the foot is currently performing. Four Parts — notice detail.
4. Finish Walking — Finish by walking normally while retaining one point of contact. Four Parts — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Finish Walking.

rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Turn attention toward the fact that experience is known.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Sensation — Choose any sensation. Notice Noticing — widen gaze.
2. Recognise — First recognise its qualities.
3. Ask Verbally — Then ask, without answering verbally, ‘How is this already known?’ Rest with the immediacy of knowing rather than searching for an object called awareness. Notice Noticing — notice detail.
4. Return Fact — Return by naming one visible fact. Notice Noticing — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Return Fact.

rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Follow Inhale → Change → Allow Breaths
rituals.goal: Rest where one phase becomes another.
rituals.mission: Rest where one phase becomes another.
rituals.challenge: Rest where one phase becomes another.
rituals.immediate_need: Rest where one phase becomes another.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Rest where one phase becomes another.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Follow Inhale — Follow a natural inhale to the instant it turns toward exhale. Breath Hinge — soften shoulders.
2. Leave Hinge Free — Do not hold or stretch the hinge.
3. Change — Notice the same effortless change at the bottom of exhalation. Breath Hinge — name sensation.
4. Allow Breaths — Visit each threshold lightly, then allow several breaths to pass unwatched. Breath Hinge — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Allow Breaths.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Trace vibration to its inner arrival point.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Listen Sustained — Listen to a sustained, gentle sound. Where Sound — hear sound.
2. Follow Apparent — Follow it from apparent distance toward the place where it becomes an auditory experience—ear, head, body, or nowhere locatable. Where Sound — notice detail.
3. Rest Briefly — When the border between outside vibration and inside hearing blurs, rest there briefly. Where Sound — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Rest Briefly.

Trace vibration to its inner arrival point.

1. Listen Sustained — Listen to a sustained, gentle sound. Where Sound — hear sound.
2. Follow Apparent — Follow it from apparent distance toward the place where it becomes an auditory experience—ear, head, body, or nowhere locatable. Where Sound — notice detail.
3. Rest Briefly — When the border between outside vibration and inside hearing blurs, rest there briefly. Where Sound — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Rest Briefly.
rituals.win_reward_source: ✓ I can trace vibration to its inner arrival point.

GOAL
Let vision teach attention another size.

rituals.name: THE BODY AS INNER SPACE
rituals.hook: Catch: Trade the sense of a solid block for a more spacious inner map.
rituals.hook_internal: Catch: Trade the sense of a solid block for a more spacious inner map.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Imagine Torso → Cavities → Keep Image

rituals.goal: Trade the sense of a solid block for a more spacious inner map.
rituals.mission: Trade the sense of a solid block for a more spacious inner map.
rituals.challenge: Trade the sense of a solid block for a more spacious inner map.
rituals.immediate_need: Trade the sense of a solid block for a more spacious inner map.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Grounding & present-moment loss

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Trade the sense of a solid block for a more spacious inner map.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Imagine Torso — Imagine the torso and limbs as volumes containing room rather than dense objects. Body As — breathe naturally.
2. Cavities — Notice cavities, distances, and open intervals inside the body mental picture while maintaining feet, seat, and external orientation in space. Body As — name sensation.
3. Keep Image — Keep the image gentle and anatomically nonliteral. Body As — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Keep Image.

✓ Trade the sense of a solid block for a more spacious inner map.

Stop immediately if the exercise increases feeling unreal or disconnected or numb unreality.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CATCH WANTING BEFORE THE OBJECT
rituals.name: CATCH WANTING BEFORE THE OBJECT
rituals.hook: Flip: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.
rituals.hook_internal: Flip: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Wait Pull → Observe Wanting → Name Object
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Wait Pull → Observe Wanting → Name Object
rituals.goal: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.
rituals.mission: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.
rituals.challenge: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.
rituals.immediate_need: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Automatic habits & autopilot

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Desire starts moving before it names a destination.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Wait Pull — Wait at the first pull: leaning, brightening, reaching, mental zoom. Catch Wanting — move slowly.
2. Observe Wanting — For five seconds, observe wanting as raw movement without completing ‘I want…’. Catch Wanting — notice detail.
3. Name Object — Only afterward name the object and decide whether pursuit serves the wider situation. Catch Wanting — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Name Object.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ Desire starts moving before it names a destination.
rituals.formula_flow: Wait Pull → Observe Wanting → Name Object
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use added support for dangerous cravings or impaired control.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.hook: Shift: The ending of pleasantness is not a failure.

rituals.mission: The ending of pleasantness is not a failure.
rituals.challenge: The ending of pleasantness is not a failure.
rituals.immediate_need: The ending of pleasantness is not a failure.
rituals.trigger_play_time:

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
The ending of pleasantness is not a failure.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Mild — Choose a mild enjoyable sensation. Watch Pleasure — widen gaze.
2. Track Rise — Track its rise, fullness, thinning, and the eventual return to neutral.
3. Resist — Resist grabbing for a second dose during the fading phase. Watch Pleasure — notice detail.
4. Pleasant — Notice what remains when the pleasant signal is gone. Watch Pleasure — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Pleasant.

rituals.name: NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST
rituals.hook: Check: Release both hands of mental grasping.
rituals.hook_internal: Check: Release both hands of mental grasping.

rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Comparison & rejection

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Release both hands of mental grasping.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Check The Pull — Notice whether experience is being pulled closer or pushed away. Against Still — press feet.
2. Relax — Relax the corresponding inner movement without demanding neutrality.
3. Let Content — Let the content remain unowned and unobstructed for a short interval. Against Still — split duty.
4. Act According — Then act according to circumstance, not attraction or aversion. Against Still — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Act According.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ Release both hands of mental grasping.
rituals.formula_flow: Check The Pull → Relax → Let Content → Act According
rituals.safety:

rituals.goal: Turn inquiry toward the assumed owner.

rituals.challenge: Turn inquiry toward the assumed owner.

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Turn inquiry toward the assumed owner.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Ask Whom — When a thought appears, ask ‘To whom did this occur?’ If ‘me’ arises, ask ‘What is this me before the answer?’ Refuse biography, role, body description, and philosophy. Who Received — move slowly.
2. Hold Question — Stay with the question’s open edge for several heartbeats. Hold Question next. Who Received — notice detail. Who Received — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Hold Question.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
See what remains when roles clock out briefly.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Name — Name the roles active today. Remove Name — move slowly.
2. Imagine Badge — One by one, imagine placing each badge on a table—parent, worker, partner, achiever, patient, helper. Remove Name — notice detail.
3. Release Roles — Sit without using any badge to answer ‘Who am I now?’ After a short pause, reclaim only the role needed next. Remove Name — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Release Roles.

rituals.title: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
rituals.name: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
rituals.ritual_name: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
rituals.hook: Look: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
rituals.hook_internal: Look: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Name Mix → Link Cue → Read Order
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Name Mix → Link Cue → Read Order
rituals.goal: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
rituals.mission: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
rituals.challenge: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
rituals.immediate_need: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Urges, impulses & cravings

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Name Mix — Name up to three present feelings. Do not explain them yet. Put Feelings — move slowly.
2. Find First — Which arrived first? Put it at the left of a short line.
3. Link Cue — Add the concrete cue that each feeling answered—words heard, an image, a body change, or a later thought. Put Feelings — name feeling.
4. Read Order — Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear. Put Feelings — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Read Order.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Mix → Find First → Link Cue → Read Order
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if sequencing pulls you into flashback, self-blame, numbness, or forced certainty about the past.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
rituals.ritual_name: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
rituals.hook: Catch: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.
rituals.hook_internal: Catch: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Wait Thought → Rest Duration → Count Gap
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Wait Thought → Rest Duration → Count Gap
rituals.goal: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.
rituals.mission: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.
rituals.challenge: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.
rituals.immediate_need: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Wait Thought — Wait for a thought to end naturally. Do Replace — breathe naturally.
2. Empty — At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest Duration — Rest for the duration available—even a fraction. Do Replace — pick action.
4. Let Thought — Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count Gap — Count the gap only after it is over. Do Replace — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Count Gap.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.
rituals.formula_flow: Wait Thought → Empty → Rest Duration → Let Thought → Count Gap
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use external engagement if silence feels frightening or destabilising.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

2. Price Trade — Choose what those three minutes will replace: rest, a message, food, movement, work, or a decision. Say the trade plainly.
3. Buy Three — If the trade is worth it, set three minutes and think only about the named question. If not, close the lap now. Pay Next — notice detail.
4. Close Toll — When the clock ends, stop without buying another lap. Do the displaced activity or deliberately let it go. Pay Next — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Close Toll.

rituals.title: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
rituals.name: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
rituals.ritual_name: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
rituals.hook: Test: Grammar can accidentally keep history live.
rituals.hook_internal: Test: Grammar can accidentally keep history live.
rituals.game_move: PLAY: Use Happened → Ground Between → Finish Moment
rituals.game_move_internal: PLAY: Use Happened → Ground Between → Finish Moment
rituals.goal: Grammar can accidentally keep history live.
rituals.mission: Grammar can accidentally keep history live.
rituals.challenge: Grammar can accidentally keep history live.
rituals.immediate_need: Grammar can accidentally keep history live.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Emotional reasoning

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Grammar can accidentally keep history live.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Use Happened — Retell one short segment using was, happened, had, and then. Put Memory — hear sound.
2. Ground Between — After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: your present location, the current year, and what choice exists now. Put Memory — name feeling.
3. Finish Moment — Finish with: ‘That ended; this moment is different.’. Put Memory — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Finish Moment.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ Grammar can accidentally keep history live.
rituals.formula_flow: Use Happened → Ground Between → Finish Moment
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not retell alone if the memory overwhelms sense of where you are.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

under 2 minutes
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Present-you should not perform every time period’s labour.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Make Time Zones — Picture three time zones: PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE. Three Selves — press feet.
2. Complete Actions — Place completed actions in PAST, available repair in PRESENT, and prevention plans in FUTURE.
3. Reassign — Move any item that belongs to the wrong time zone. Three Selves — pick action.
4. Perform — Perform only one PRESENT task now. Three Selves — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Perform.

rituals.goal: Put the real years back between then and now.

rituals.immediate_need: Put the real years back between then and now.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Put the real years back between then and now.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Date Events — Picture the dates of the events that currently feel piled together. Put Years — soften shoulders.
2. Scale Distance — Give equal physical space to equal spans of time; do not place every event in one crowded cluster.
3. Present — Notice TODAY at the correct distance and name one fact that belongs only to now. Put Years — pick action.
4. Recheck Urgency — Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored. Put Years — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Recheck Urgency.

✓ I can put the real years back between then and now.

rituals.hook: Play: Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.

rituals.game_move: PLAY: Describe Event → Return Person → Distance

rituals.challenge: Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.

rituals.trigger_play_time:

GOAL
Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Every identity grants permissions and charges fees.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Sort Identity Costs — Imagine three buckets: IT LETS ME; IT STOPS ME; IT DEMANDS FROM ME. Price Keeping — loosen hands.
2. Fill The Buckets — Mentally sort the self-concept into those three buckets. Price Keeping — pick action.
3. Find The Price — Focus on the highest hidden cost and ask whether the identity still earns its keep. Price Keeping — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Find The Price.

rituals.goal: The remembered self deserves credible rethought.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
The remembered self deserves credible rethought.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Introduce — Introduce a compassionate observer appropriate to the event—a trusted adult, advocate, elder, clinician, or current-you. Add Witness — press feet.

3. Keep Words — Keep their words believable. Add Witness — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Keep Words.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Different uncertainties require different responses.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Classify — Categorise the unknown: answerable now, answerable later, influenceable but unknowable, or permanently unknowable. Species Unknown — feel support.
2. Apply Move — Apply its matching move—research, schedule, act on influence, or practise acceptance. Species Unknown — allow opposite.
3. Use Category — Refuse to use one category’s tool on another. Species Unknown — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Use Category.

rituals.goal: Uncertainty need not prevent preparation.
rituals.mission: Uncertainty need not prevent preparation.

rituals.trigger_play_time:

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Uncertainty need not prevent preparation.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Plausible — Choose two plausible outcomes and build a short branch for each: first signal, first action, resource, and exit. Plan Both — loosen hands.
2. Prepare Both — Prepare any step useful in both branches now. Plan Both — allow opposite.
3. Select Path — Delay preference until evidence selects the path. Plan Both — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Select Path.

items.name: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
items.hook: Shift: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
items.hook_internal: Shift: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
items.game_move: PLAY: Keep Event → Predict Different → Speak Plurals
items.game_move_internal: PLAY: Keep Event → Predict Different → Speak Plurals
items.goal: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
items.mission: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
items.challenge: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
items.immediate_need: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Catastrophic prediction

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Keep Event — Keep the event fixed. Three Worlds — widen gaze.
2. Invent — Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Predict Different — Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next. Three Worlds — challenge answer.
4. Earliest — Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Speak Plurals — Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy. Three Worlds — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Speak Plurals.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
items.formula_flow: Keep Event → Invent → Predict Different → Earliest → Speak Plurals
items.safety:
PAUSE
Do not multiply theories when an urgent practical response is already clear.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Prefix Thought — Take the exact thought and place these words before it: ‘I am noticing my mind produce…’ Say the complete sentence once at ordinary speed. Add Prefix — breathe naturally.
2. Check Command — Notice what remains true and what loses command authority. Add Prefix — pick action.
3. Resume Task — Carry on with the next chosen task while the sentence exists nearby. Add Prefix — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Resume Task.

items.safety:

Drop the wording if it feels mocking, unreal, or destabilising.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

Rigid beliefs, labels & stories

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Give thought transport, not a throne.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Place Thought — Place the thought on something already moving: a bus passing, a leaf in drainage water, subtitles leaving a screen. Thought Departures — soften shoulders.
2. Watch Arrival — Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. Return Eyes — When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one stationary object. Thought Departures — allow opposite.
4. Allow Departure — Another vehicle may come; none owns the station. Thought Departures — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Allow Departure.

GOAL
Separate the wound from the fist wrapped around it.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Make Two Lanes — Imagine two lanes: WHAT HURTS and WHAT RESISTANCE ADDS. Pain Plus — soften shoulders.
2. Keep The Hurt — In the first lane, picture the raw sensation or fact.
3. Catch The Fight — In the second lane, name demands, self-attack, bracing, and impossible arguments with reality. Pain Plus — split duty.
4. Drop One Fight — Release one item from the resistance lane while respecting the hurt. Pain Plus — next action.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Ordinary — Choose one ordinary activity. Enter Action — feel support.
2. Place Vision — Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. Leave Re — When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself. Enter Action — allow opposite.
4. Stay Activity — Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Participation — Participation, not perfect focus, is the target. Enter Action — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Participation.

items.title: THE ATTENTION BOUNCER
items.name: THE ATTENTION BOUNCER
items.hook: Flip: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
items.hook_internal: Flip: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
items.game_move: PLAY: Spot Arrival → Set Budget → Return Door
items.game_move_internal: PLAY: Spot Arrival → Set Budget → Return Door
items.goal: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
items.mission: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
items.challenge: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
items.immediate_need: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Spot Arrival — Notice the next thought without following it. Attention Bouncer — move slowly.
2. Stamp Access — Stamp it REQUESTED, RELEVANT, or UNINVITED.
3. Set Budget — Give only the chosen category a short timer; let the others wait without argument. Attention Bouncer — notice detail.
4. Return Door — When the timer ends, return to the task or deliberately admit one new thought. Attention Bouncer — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Return Door.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
items.formula_flow: Spot Arrival → Stamp Access → Set Budget → Return Door
items.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the labels become a checking ritual or make urgent action harder.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

items.hook: Zoom: Feelings move differently when they are not put on trial.

items.immediate_need: Feelings move differently when they are not put on trial.

TRIGGER
Body-state misreading

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Feelings move differently when they are not put on trial.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Locate Emotion — Locate the emotion in the body and give it a precise name. Emotion Complete — loosen hands.
2. Permit — Permit its current intensity without feeding the story.
3. Track Sensation — Track where sensation travels, peaks, breaks, or cools. Emotion Complete — notice detail.
4. Follow Appears — Follow until one natural shift appears, then choose the action the situation—not the wave—requires. Emotion Complete — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Follow Appears.

items.title: ONE CLEAN WISH
items.name: ONE CLEAN WISH
items.hook: Shift: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
items.hook_internal: Shift: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
items.game_move: PLAY: Bring Person → State Boundary → Keep Discernment
items.game_move_internal: PLAY: Bring Person → State Boundary → Keep Discernment
items.goal: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
items.mission: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
items.challenge: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
items.immediate_need: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Boundaries & over-responsibility

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Bring Person — Bring the person to mind at a safe distance. Clean Wish — widen gaze.
2. Keep It Honest — Choose one honest wish that does not deny harm: ‘May we both be free from causing more suffering,’ or ‘May safety become possible.’ Offer it once.
3. State Boundary — Then state the boundary or action you still need. Clean Wish — split duty.
4. Keep Discernment — Warmth does not cancel discernment. Clean Wish — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Keep Discernment.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
items.formula_flow: Bring Person → Keep It Honest → State Boundary → Keep Discernment
items.safety:
PAUSE
Do not direct compassion exercises toward an abuser if it weakens necessary distance.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

items.title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
items.name: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
items.hook: Look: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
items.hook_internal: Look: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
items.game_move: PLAY: Set Code → Reverse Code → Claim Control
items.game_move_internal: PLAY: Set Code → Reverse Code → Claim Control
items.goal: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
items.mission: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
items.challenge: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
items.immediate_need: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and look at one fixed object. Say the order once. Play Body — hear sound.
2. Run Order — Perform A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — Perform C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, return to neutral and restart instead of speeding up. Play Body — name sensation.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the whole code stop. Play Body — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Claim Control.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
items.formula_flow: Set Code → Run Order → Reverse Code → Claim Control
items.safety:
PAUSE
Do not play while driving, moving through hazards, dizzy, injured, or unable to stay oriented.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

items.name: THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE
items.hook: Bet: Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.
items.hook_internal: Bet: Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.
items.game_move: PLAY: Stop Nonessential → Observe Facts → Skip Negotiation

items.mission: Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.
items.challenge: Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.
items.immediate_need: Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Urges, impulses & cravings

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Stop Nonessential — S — stop every nonessential movement. Four Letter — feel support.
2. Take Physical — T — take one physical step back.
3. Observe Facts — O — observe facts, sensations, and the strongest impulse. Four Letter — name feeling.
4. Proceed Safely — P — proceed with the smallest safe move that will still make sense in an hour.
5. Skip Negotiation — Do not negotiate with momentum between letters. Four Letter — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Skip Negotiation.

items.mission: Hold distress and safety in the same frame.
items.challenge: Hold distress and safety in the same frame.
items.immediate_need: Hold distress and safety in the same frame.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Trauma & memory-as-present

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Hold distress and safety in the same frame.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Stable — Choose a stable anchor such as feet on the floor or a fixed sound. Foot Here — press feet.
2. Keep Most — Keep most attention there while allowing a small edge of distress into awareness.
3. Anchor Verify — Verify the anchor remains present. Foot Here — name sensation.
4. Adjust — Adjust the ratio until both can coexist without losing choice. Foot Here — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Adjust.

items.hook_internal: Notice: A large release can become several manageable ones.

items.game_move_internal: PLAY: Let Air → Keep Face → Wait Body
items.goal: A large release can become several manageable ones.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A large release can become several manageable ones.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Let Air — Instead of one continuous out-breath, let air leave in three soft portions with tiny unforced spaces between. Exhale Chapters — breathe naturally.
2. Keep Face — Keep the face loose and never push to empty. Exhale Chapters — name sensation.
3. Wait Body — After the final segment, wait for the body’s next inhale rather than grabbing it. Exhale Chapters — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Wait Body.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ A large release can become several manageable ones.
items.formula_flow: Let Air → Keep Face → Wait Body
items.safety:
PAUSE
Resume normal breathing if segmentation causes urgency or tingling.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

items.goal_why_game_move:

items.play_the_loop:
1. Open Field — Open Field with sight, sound, sensation, and thought available at once. Let Field — widen gaze.
2. Whatever — Notice whatever becomes prominent, then what replaces it.
3. Let All Arrive — Do not select, rank, or hold any item. Let Field — allow opposite.
4. Track Changing — Track the changing editorial order for one minute. Let Field — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Track Changing.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL

items.play_the_loop:
1. Let Field — Let the field choose its next foreground. No Favourite — soften shoulders.
2. Pleasant — Pleasant, unpleasant, dull, or vivid—offer each the same brief hospitality.
3. Include Movement — When preference reaches to grip or reject, include that movement too. No Favourite — notice detail.
4. End Whole — End by noticing the whole room at once. No Favourite — next action.

⚡ FINISH — End Whole.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Grounding & present-moment loss

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Make the present answer in specifics.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Find Five — Find five distinct colours or shapes, four contact sensations, three separate sounds, two scents, and one taste or mouth sensation. Sense Roll — feel support.
2. Answer Blue — No generic answers; ‘blue attention’ beats ‘something blue.’ Let the inventory end with the most stable item. Answer Blue next. Sense Roll — name sensation. Sense Roll — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Answer Blue.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Body-state misreading

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Move awareness through an hourglass.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Acknowledge — First, acknowledge the full weather of the moment. Expand Gather — press feet.
2. Breathe Small — Next, gather attention around breathing as a small centre.
3. Widen Whole — Finally, widen to the whole body and surrounding space. Expand Gather — notice detail.
4. Spend — Spend roughly one minute in each shape.
5. Carry Final — Carry the final wide frame into your next movement. Expand Gather — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Carry Final.

items.hook: Probe: Walking can become a moving attention track.
items.hook_internal: Probe: Walking can become a moving attention track.
items.game_move: PLAY: Place Weight → Thought → Finish Walking
items.game_move_internal: PLAY: Place Weight → Thought → Finish Walking
items.goal: Walking can become a moving attention track.

items.trigger_play_time:

Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Walking can become a moving attention track.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Place Weight — Slow enough to distinguish lift, travel, place, and weight transfer. Four Parts — move slowly.
2. Follow Events — Follow those four events through several steps.
3. Thought — When thought pulls away, rejoin at whichever phase the foot is currently performing. Four Parts — notice detail.
4. Finish Walking — Finish by walking normally while retaining one point of contact. Four Parts — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Finish Walking.

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Turn attention toward the fact that experience is known.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Sensation — Choose any sensation. Notice Noticing — widen gaze.
2. Recognise — First recognise its qualities.
3. Ask Verbally — Then ask, without answering verbally, ‘How is this already known?’ Rest with the immediacy of knowing rather than searching for an object called awareness. Notice Noticing — notice detail.
4. Return Fact — Return by naming one visible fact. Notice Noticing — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Return Fact.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Desire starts moving before it names a destination.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Wait Pull — Wait at the first pull: leaning, brightening, reaching, mental zoom. Catch Wanting — move slowly.
2. Observe Wanting — For five seconds, observe wanting as raw movement without completing ‘I want…’. Catch Wanting — notice detail.
3. Name Object — Only afterward name the object and decide whether pursuit serves the wider situation. Catch Wanting — next action.

items.title: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
items.name: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
items.ritual_name: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
items.hook: Look: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
items.hook_internal: Look: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
items.game_move: PLAY: Name Mix → Link Cue → Read Order
items.game_move_internal: PLAY: Name Mix → Link Cue → Read Order
items.goal: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
items.mission: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
items.challenge: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
items.immediate_need: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Urges, impulses & cravings

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Name Mix — Name up to three present feelings. Do not explain them yet. Put Feelings — move slowly.
2. Find First — Which arrived first? Put it at the left of a short line.
3. Link Cue — Add the concrete cue that each feeling answered—words heard, an image, a body change, or a later thought. Put Feelings — name feeling.
4. Read Order — Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear. Put Feelings — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Read Order.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
items.formula_flow: Name Mix → Find First → Link Cue → Read Order
items.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if sequencing pulls you into flashback, self-blame, numbness, or forced certainty about the past.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

items.game_move: PLAY: Name Lap → Buy Three → Close Toll

items.goal: Another thought is not free when it spends the next three minutes of your life.
items.mission: Another thought is not free when it spends the next three minutes of your life.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Rumination & worry loops

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Another thought is not free when it spends the next three minutes of your life.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Name Lap — Name the exact question you want one more thinking lap to answer. One sentence only. Pay Next — hear sound.
2. Price Trade — Choose what those three minutes will replace: rest, a message, food, movement, work, or a decision. Say the trade plainly.
3. Buy Three — If the trade is worth it, set three minutes and think only about the named question. If not, close the lap now. Pay Next — notice detail.
4. Close Toll — When the clock ends, stop without buying another lap. Do the displaced activity or deliberately let it go. Pay Next — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Close Toll.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ I just noticed the loop before giving it another lap.
items.formula_flow: Name Lap → Price Trade → Buy Three → Close Toll
items.safety:
PAUSE
Never buy another analysis lap with sleep, medication, food, immediate safety, or time-critical responsibilities.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

TRIGGER

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Grammar can accidentally keep history live.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Use Happened — Retell one short segment using was, happened, had, and then. Put Memory — hear sound.
2. Ground Between — After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: your present location, the current year, and what choice exists now. Put Memory — name feeling.
3. Finish Moment — Finish with: ‘That ended; this moment is different.’. Put Memory — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Finish Moment.

items.title: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
items.name: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
items.ritual_name: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
items.hook: Notice: Put the real years back between then and now.
items.hook_internal: Notice: Put the real years back between then and now.
items.game_move: PLAY: Date Events → Present → Recheck Urgency
items.game_move_internal: PLAY: Date Events → Present → Recheck Urgency
items.goal: Put the real years back between then and now.
items.mission: Put the real years back between then and now.
items.challenge: Put the real years back between then and now.
items.immediate_need: Put the real years back between then and now.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Urgency & decision pressure

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Put the real years back between then and now.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Date Events — Picture the dates of the events that currently feel piled together. Put Years — soften shoulders.
2. Scale Distance — Give equal physical space to equal spans of time; do not place every event in one crowded cluster.
3. Present — Notice TODAY at the correct distance and name one fact that belongs only to now. Put Years — pick action.
4. Recheck Urgency — Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored. Put Years — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Recheck Urgency.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
✓ I can put the real years back between then and now.
items.formula_flow: Date Events → Scale Distance → Present → Recheck Urgency
items.safety:
PAUSE
Stop and reorient to the room if the timeline makes the past feel more present.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Identity verbs can turn weather into a prison.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Drop Identity Verb — Restate ‘I am broken/lazy/anxious’ without am or is. Delete Am — press feet.
2. Use Temporary — Use temporary action language: ‘Avoiding has increased this week,’ ‘Anxiety is moving through the chest,’ ‘Energy dropped after…’. Delete Am — name feeling.
3. Add Condition — Add one condition under which the process changes. Delete Am — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Add Condition.

PLAY TIME

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Describe Event — Frame the moment once as ‘this mind is predicting…’ or ‘the system is producing…’. Third Person — breathe naturally.
2. Change — Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
3. Return Person — Then return to first person for the action you genuinely own: ‘I will…’. Third Person — pick action.
4. Distance — Distance the content, not agency. Third Person — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Distance.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Evidence distortion & selective thinking

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Attention needs more than one focal length.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Object — Select an object. Zoom Lens — widen gaze.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Every identity grants permissions and charges fees.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Sort Identity Costs — Imagine three buckets: IT LETS ME; IT STOPS ME; IT DEMANDS FROM ME. Price Keeping — loosen hands.
2. Fill The Buckets — Mentally sort the self-concept into those three buckets. Price Keeping — pick action.
3. Find The Price — Focus on the highest hidden cost and ask whether the identity still earns its keep. Price Keeping — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Find The Price.

items.hook: Peek: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.

items.game_move: PLAY: Give Self → Protect Whole → Chair

items.goal: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
items.mission: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
items.challenge: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
items.immediate_need: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Give Self — Give each self-state a seat. Call Inner — feel support.
2. Sentence — One sentence each: what I need, what I fear, what I propose.
3. Protect Whole — Appoint a chair whose job is to protect the whole system over time. Call Inner — pick action.
4. Chair — The chair may combine, delay, or reject proposals, but must acknowledge every need. Call Inner — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Chair.

items.goal: The remembered self deserves credible rethought.

TRIGGER

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
The remembered self deserves credible rethought.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Introduce — Introduce a compassionate observer appropriate to the event—a trusted adult, advocate, elder, clinician, or current-you. Add Witness — press feet.
2. Name Wrong — Have them name what was wrong, what protection was deserved, and what is true about the person who endured it. Add Witness — notice detail.
3. Keep Words — Keep their words believable. Add Witness — next action.

⚡ FINISH — Keep Words.
